counterexample: Use the proof's own model: A=B=0, C=1, with two independent uniform calls on [0,1]. Greedy dispatch has expected total cost ∫_0^{1/2}(x+1/4)dx + ∫_{1/2}^1(3/2-x)dx = 5/8 = 40/64. Instead, dispatch a left ambulance when the first call x≤5/8 and dispatch C when x>5/8; then dispatch the nearest remaining ambulance. Its expected total cost is ∫_0^{5/8}(x+1/4)dx + ∫_{5/8}^1(3/2-x)dx = 39/64, strictly less than 40/64. For example, at x=3/5, C is closest, but sending a left ambulance gives conditional expected total cost 3/5+1/4=17/20, versus 1-3/5+1/2=9/10 from sending C.
assessment_summary: Step 0011 is false. The proof compares greedy only with the policy that always dispatches A first, overlooking intermediate policies that preserve C only for some right-half calls. The threshold policy above strictly improves the expected response time.
